newsitem.title: INDONESIA: INDONESIAN STOCKS - factors to watch - Dec 27.
newsitem.headline: INDONESIAN STOCKS - factors to watch - Dec 27.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors likely to affect Indonesian stocks on Friday:

* Indonesia's economy was expected to grow by between 7.6 and 8.0 percent in 1997 while inflation was seen at below 7.0 percent. This year the economy is expected to expand by 7.6-7.9 percent, with inflation seen at 6.5-6.8 percent. The forecast was made by the Industry and Trade Ministry on Thursday.

* Indonesia's non-oil and gas imports were expected to total between $43.8 billion and $44.2 billion in 1997, up from an estimated total of between $39.2 billion and $39.6 billion this year. Its non-oil and gas exports were expected to total between $44.7 billion and $45.1 billion in 1997, compared with between $38.8 billion and $39.1 billion this year.
* The Dow industrial rose 23.83 points to 6,546.68 on Thursday, leaving the index of 30 blue-chip stocks just shy of its record of 6,547.79 set on November 25.

* An Indonesian mob, apparently incensed by the alleged beating of a religious teacher by police, went on a rampage on Thursday in the West Java town of Tasikmalaya, setting fire to churches, commercial buildings and vehicles, police and residents said.
* The Jakarta Composite Index fell 0.25 points, or 0.04 percent, to close at 632.50 points on Thursday after some window-dressing spurred fresh buying in late trading.
* On Friday, the rupiah was quoted at 2,362.75/63.50 in early trading against the opening of 2,362.00/63.00.

* Bank Bira on reports that a subsidiary of General Electric Co of the United States had bought a seven percent stake in the bank and that Bank Bira expected to post a net profit of 60 billion rupiah in 1996 against 30.34 billion rupiah last year.
* Chicken restaurant franchiser Putra Sejahtera Pioneerindo on market talk that a foreign investor was interested in buying a stake in the firm.
* Bimantara on announcement that the conglomerate had increased its stake in PT Nestle Indonesia to 19.95 percent from 13.72 percent.
* Textile manufacturer Karwell Indonesia on announcement it had link up with PT Ladang Kreasi Dwiperkasa to boost sales.
* Trading firm Rimba Niaga Idola on announcement it had postponed indefinitely plans to acquire privately-owned PT Transco Multisindo and for a rights issue.
